Quezon City www_dilq.qcvpn CILG OPINION NO. 30 S. MAR 08 MR. AZUCENA C. MAMPO Former Sangguniang Barangay Member Barangay San Agustin, Municipality of Canaman Province of Camarines Sur azucenamampo@gmail.com Dear Mr. Mampo This has reference to your electronic mail dated 29 November 2023 seeking the Department's legal opinion regarding the convening of the newly-elected sangguniang barangay members without conducting a mass oath taking of office. According to the representation, you were unsuccessful in your bid for sangguniang barangay member in the most recent Barangay-Sangguniang Kabataan Elections 2023 in your barangay. You represented that on November 6, 2023, the members of the last sangguniang barangay convened as part of the regular session and agreed that you would hold your final regular session on November 13, 2023. However, you stated that on November 9, 2023, the newly elected sangguniang barangay members convened without informing the members of the last sangguniang barangay. Thus, you are seeking legal opinion on the following: I. Whether the newly elected officials can convene or meet even without submitting the Statement of Contributions and Expenditures (SOCE); 2. Whether the newly elected officials are required to take the oath of office simultaneously; and 3. Entitlement to honorarium and SRI In reply to your first query, we invite your attention to section 14 of Republic Act No. 71661 which provides that every candidate should file a SOCE with COMELEC within thirty (30) days after the day of the election, and before entering upon the duties of his office, if elected, to wit: 1 Entitled, An Act Providing for Synchronized National and Local Elections and for Electoral Reforms, Authorizing Appropriations Therefor, and for Other Purposes "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"SEC. 14. Statement of Contributions and Expenditures: Effect of Failure to File Statement. — Every candidate and treasurer of the political party shall, within thirty (30) days after the day of the election, file in duplicate with the offices of the Commission the full, true and itemized statement of all contributions and expenditures in connection with the election. No person elected to any public office shall enter upon the duties of his office until he has filed the statement of contributions and expenditures herein required. XXX" (Emphasis supplied) From the foregoing, it is evident that a newly-elected official shall not enter upon the duties of his/her office or assume said office until he or she has filed the appropriate SOCE. In the matter at hand, it was unclear whether the newly elected members of the sangguniang barangay met for their first regular session or just a simple gathering. Hence, we opted to limit the discussion on Section 14 of Republic Act No. 7166 only. Given that you said that the newly-elected members of the sangguniang barangay have not yet filed the required SOCE, they are not yet permitted to perform the duties of their office, including convening for a regular session. However, nothing in the law that forbids the newly-elected officials from convening if it is only a simple meeting of the members, and not yet a regular session. As to the second query, we answer in the negative. Please be advised that nothing in the law or the omnibus election code compels or precludes newly elected officials from taking their oaths of office simultaneously. In fact, Section 92 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) states that all elective and appointive local officials and employees shall, upon assumption to office, subscribe to an oath or affirmation of office in the prescribed form. The oath or affirmation of office shall be filed with the office of the local chief executive concerned. As the entitlement of SRI, please be informed that the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) has already clarified this matter. In its letter dated December 29, 2023, it emphasized Item 8.0 of DBM Budget Circular (BC) No. 2023-22 which provides that the grant of one-time SRI to employees in LGUs, including those in the barangays, shall be determined by their respective sanggunians depending on the LGU's financial capability, at a uniform rate not exceeding Twenty Thousand Pesos (P20,OOO.OO) each, subject to among others, adherence to the guidelines on the grant of the SRI under Item 5.0 of BC No. 2023-2 (Item 8.2 thereof). It bears stressing that the specific amount of the SRI in the barangays shall be determined by their respective sanggunians based on the LGU's financial capability and subject to the Personnel Services limitation prescribed under the LGC. Hence, appointive and elective officials who are in the service as of November 30, 2023 may be entitled to the grant of the one-time SRI, whether in full amount or on pro-rated basis, depending on their respective lengths of rendered services this year. 2 Entitled, Guidelines on the Grant of Service Recognition Incentive to Government Employees for FY 2023 Page 2 of 3

Conversely, the LGU officials who formerly occupied positions but are no longer in office as of November 30, 2023 are not entitled to the grant of the FY 2023 SRI. For newly elected individuals, i.e. those who won after the October 30, 3023 local election, the respective officials in the barangay concerned are in a better position to assess their performance, in order to be entitled to the pro-rated SRI (i.e., 10% for less than one month of service. As to entitlement of honorarium it bears to note that under DBM Local Budget Circular No. 63, in relation to Section 393 of the Local Government Code, Sangguniang Barangay Members are paid in the form of honorarium. Corollary thereto, the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual defines honorarium as that renumeraion given to a public official for services actually rendered. Hence, the grant of honorarium is based principally on services actually rendered by the claimant thereof. Accordingly, other than other certain factors, the most convenient way of measuring the services actually rendered by a Sangguniang Barangay Member is attendance in sessions. Under the Local Government Code, Sangguniang Barangays are mandated to conduct two sessions a month. The honorarium can, therefore, be divided into two parts, each representing each session. Hence, if a Sangguniang Barangay Member will absent himself from sessions, he is not entitled to receive the proportionate amount of honorarium for services actually rendered, If he will be absent in both sessions for one month, then he can be deprived of hid total honorarium for that month3. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same, and is without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, Y THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AT CTOR R.
